mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period signals worsening labor market conditions, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to economic deterioration.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment (PAYEMS) and rises in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a deteriorating labor market, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings face headwinds from reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-recession recovery regime, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 3-month moving average signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which correlates with rising corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 3-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above its 4-quarter moving average indicates a strengthening economy, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 > 4-quarter moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates weakening demand for housing and consumer goods, which correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST declines and RSAFS declines, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime, a federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.0% signals restrictive policy, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as higher borrowing costs dampen economic growth and corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.
